title: Fix Flaky Saga Test — Replace time.Sleep with Channel Sync
description:
**Problem**: `TestSagaRollback` uses `time.Sleep(50ms)` for synchronization, causing CI flakes.

**Fix**: Replace with channel-based sync and `assert.Eventually`.

**Files**: `core/controlplane/scheduler/saga_test.go`
definitionOfDone: Replaced with channel-based synchronization or assert.Eventually
Test passes reliably: go test -run TestSagaRollback -count=10

implementationPlan.description:
Step 1: Fix TestSagaRollbackRespectsContextTimeout in saga_test.go

Line 228-229 uses `time.Sleep(1ms)` to ensure a nanosecond-timeout fires. Replace with a pre-cancelled context pattern:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
cancel() // already cancelled
```
This is deterministic — no timing dependency.
implementationPlan.note: Replaced 1ns timeout + 1ms sleep with pre-cancelled context (WithCancel + immediate cancel). Removed unused time import.

implementationPlan.description:
Step 2: Fix engine_test.go poll-loop for saga rollback dispatch

Lines 483-489 in TestHandleJobResultTriggersRollback uses poll-loop with `time.Sleep(10ms)`. Replace with `assert.Eventually` or extend the deadline and use a channel-based notification pattern. Since the rollback is fired in a goroutine (line 638-649 in engine.go), the poll loop is necessary but should use `testing.T.Deadline()` or a generous timeout with `assert.Eventually`.

Replace with:
```go
assert.Eventually(t, func() bool {
    return len(bus.published) > 0
}, 2*time.Second, 10*time.Millisecond)
```
Add `github.com/stretchr/testify/assert` import if not already present, or use a manual eventually helper.
implementationPlan.note: Replaced poll-loop with time.Sleep(10ms) with context-based ticker pattern using 2s timeout. Uses context.WithTimeout + ticker.C select to wait for bus.published, with clear fatal on timeout.

implementationPlan.description:
Step 3: Verify tests pass reliably

Run `go test -run TestSagaRollback -count=10 ./core/controlplane/scheduler/...` and `go test -run TestHandleJobResultTriggersRollback -count=10 ./core/controlplane/scheduler/...` to confirm reliability. Then full suite: `go test ./core/controlplane/scheduler/... -count=3`.
